reports.title: ACS - Class Wide Project 1 - SIMD Advantage Profiling

figures.caption: Fig. 1. SIMD speedup (scalar time / auto-vectorized time) across working-set sizes. Higher is faster; 1× means equal performance. Bands show the interquartile range, and cache markers indicate nominal capacities.
Fig. 2. Scalar and auto-vectorized throughput across working-set sizes. GFLOP/s measures billions of floating-point operations per second; higher is faster. Bands show the interquartile range.
Fig. 3. Geometric-mean scalar-to-auto speedup across the three kernels for aligned and shifted arrays. Higher is faster; 1× means equal performance.
Fig. 4. Geometric-mean scalar-to-auto speedup across the three kernels at an original array length of 32,768 elements, comparing aligned, shifted, tail-only, and combined conditions.
Fig. 5. AXPY scalar-to-auto speedup by stride; dashed line: equal performance (1×); bands: interquartile range.
Fig. 6. Useful bandwidth by stride for arrays that fit in L2 cache (top) and arrays requiring main-memory access (bottom). Higher is faster. Bands show the interquartile range.
Fig. 7. Dot-product time per element with strict and relaxed floating-point summation. Lower is faster. Error bars show the interquartile range.

Fig. 8. Scalar and auto-vectorized SAXPY throughput compared with the estimated memory-bandwidth limit. Bars show medians, error bars show interquartile ranges, and shading shows the interquartile range of the estimated limit.
Fig. 9. Core cycles per element. Lower is better. Bands show the interquartile range. K = 1,024 and M = 1,048,576 elements.

reports.title: ACS - Class Wide Project 2 - Cache & Memory Performance Profiling

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Random dependent-load latency for four representative spans. Lower is faster. Bars show medians; error bars show interquartile ranges.
Fig. 2a. Pointer latency and useful transfer bandwidth across a 96 MiB span. Lower latency and higher bandwidth are better. Bands show interquartile ranges.
Fig. 2b. Paired random/sequential bandwidth at four-times spacing. Values below 1× favor sequential access. Error bars show interquartile ranges; open markers show round medians.
Fig. 3. Bandwidth and average block-processing time across read/write mixes. The horizontal axis gives the write percentage. Bands show interquartile ranges.
Fig. 4a. Throughput and mean chain round-trip time versus physical-core count and independent-chain count. Bands show interquartile ranges.
Fig. 4b. Throughput versus mean chain round-trip time. Bars show interquartile ranges on both axes; lines follow increasing concurrency. Labels identify selected chain counts.
Fig. 5. Latency and completed-load throughput across working-set sizes. Bands show interquartile ranges. Dashed lines mark nominal cache capacities; shading marks spans larger than L3.

Fig. 6a. Measured full-hierarchy AMAT components. Points show medians; bands show interquartile ranges. Open markers indicate uncertain estimates; gaps indicate missing classes. Dashed lines mark nominal cache capacities.
Fig. 6b. Reconstructed AMAT and independently timed access. Bands show interquartile ranges across 30 paired trials. Open markers indicate uncertain components; no values were fitted or filled in.
Fig. 7. Latency and dTLB read misses with normal and verified huge pages. Bands show interquartile ranges. Miss-count panels use different vertical scales.
Fig. 8. Useful read bandwidth for reused 32 KiB and 192 MiB buffers. Bars show medians; error bars show interquartile ranges.

reports.title: ACS - Class Wide Project 3 - SSD Performance Profiling

figures.caption: Fig. 1. QD 1 latency for four baseline workloads over 1 GiB. Bars show medians; error bars show trial IQRs. Lower is faster.
Fig. 2. Read throughput and latency versus block size at QD 16 over 1 GiB. Lines show medians of five paired trials; bands show IQRs.
Fig. 3. Throughput and mean latency versus write percentage; 4 KiB random I/O, QD 16, 1 GiB. Bands show trial IQRs.
Fig. 4a. Average requests in flight calculated per trial as IOPS × mean latency in seconds, compared with requested QD. Error bars show IQRs.
Fig. 4b. Throughput versus mean latency for 4 KiB random reads over 1 GiB. Labels identify QD; bars show IQRs on both axes. The marked knee uses the 90%-of-peak criterion.
Fig. 5. Total I/O latency percentiles for 4 KiB random reads at QD 8 and QD 32. Points show medians of five per-trial percentiles; bands show IQRs.
Fig. 6. Random-read latency and throughput versus file range; 4 KiB requests, QD 16. Lines show eight-trial medians, bands show IQRs, and faint points show individual trials.
Fig. 7. Mean throughput and latency across five 60-second write bursts; 128 KiB sequential writes, QD 16, 16 GiB. Each plotted window averages five runs.
Fig. 8. Repeated 128 KiB reads over 16 MiB at QD 1, comparing buffered and direct I/O. Bars show five-trial medians; error bars show IQRs.
